statement: You are given an integer n. Return how many prime numbers are strictly less than n.

The Sieve of Eratosthenes does this efficiently: assume every number from 2 to n − 1 is prime, then for each p that is still marked prime, cross out its multiples starting from p × p. The numbers left unmarked are the primes.

examples.explanation: There are no primes below 1, since the smallest prime is 2.
